title: Procedural Mini Golf with Ferrari Obstacle
prompt:
Create a single HTML file implementing a procedural mini golf game using Three.js with the following detailed specifications:

## Scene Setup
- Use Three.js with OrbitControls and GLTFLoader from CDN
- Create a perspective camera at position (0, 12, 15) looking at the origin
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light at (10, 20, 10) with intensity 1.0 and shadow mapping enabled
- Sky-blue background color (#87CEEB)

## Golf Course (Procedural)
- Generate a flat rectangular green course (20 units long x 8 units wide) using a BoxGeometry with green material (#2d8a4e), positioned at y=0
- Add raised border walls (0.3 units tall, brown #8B4513) around all four edges of the course
- Place a circular hole at position (0, 0.01, -7) with radius 0.4, using a dark material (#111111). Use a CylinderGeometry sunk into the ground.
- Add a flag pole at the hole: thin cylinder (radius 0.05, height 2) with a small red triangular flag (PlaneGeometry) at the top
- Create 2 rectangular obstacle bumpers on the course: one at (-2, 0.25, -3) size (3, 0.5, 0.5) and another at (1.5, 0.25, -5) size (2.5, 0.5, 0.5), both colored #666666

## Ferrari Obstacle
- Load 'ferrari.glb' using GLTFLoader and place it at position (0, 0.5, -1) on the course
- Scale the Ferrari model to fit reasonably on the course (scale 0.8)
- The Ferrari acts as a physical obstacle - the ball must bounce off it
- Slowly rotate the Ferrari around Y-axis (0.3 rad/s) to make it a dynamic obstacle

## Golf Ball
- White sphere (radius 0.2) starting at position (0, 0.2, 6) - the tee position
- Implement simple 2D physics for the ball on the XZ plane:
  - Velocity-based movement with friction (multiply velocity by 0.985 each frame)
  - Ball stops when speed < 0.01 (set velocity to zero)
  - Collision with border walls: reflect velocity component and multiply by 0.7 (energy loss)
  - Collision with obstacle bumpers: AABB collision, reflect appropriate velocity component, multiply by 0.7
  - Collision with Ferrari: use distance-based sphere collision (radius 1.5 from Ferrari center), reflect velocity away from Ferrari center, multiply by 0.6
  - Hole detection: when ball center is within 0.5 units of hole center AND ball speed < 2.0, the ball falls in (move to hole position, set velocity to zero, increment score)

## Shot Mechanic
- When ball is stationary, player can aim and shoot:
- Show an aiming arrow (ArrowHelper) from ball position. The arrow direction is controlled by LEFT/RIGHT arrow keys (rotate aim angle by 0.05 rad per keypress)
- Shot power is controlled by holding SPACE: power increases from 0 to 10 over 2 seconds while held, displayed on a power bar in the HUD
- On SPACE release, apply velocity to ball in the aim direction multiplied by power value
- Each shot increments the stroke counter
- Hide the aiming arrow while ball is moving

## Game State & HUD
- Display a HUD overlay (HTML div) showing:
  - Current hole: 'Hole 1' (top-left)
  - Strokes: count of shots taken (top-left, below hole)
  - Power bar: a colored bar (green->yellow->red gradient based on power level), 200px wide, 20px tall, bottom-center
  - Status message: center-top, shows 'Aim and shoot!' when ready, 'Ball in motion...' when moving, 'HOLE IN ONE!' or 'Hole Complete! Strokes: N' when ball sinks
- A 'Reset Ball' button (top-right) that returns ball to tee position and resets velocity
- A 'New Course' button (below Reset) that randomizes obstacle positions (within course bounds) and resets everything

## State Management (CRITICAL)
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ object updated every frame with:
  - ballPosition: {x, y, z} current ball position
  - ballVelocity: {x, y, z} current ball velocity
  - ballSpeed: magnitude of velocity
  - ballMoving: boolean, true if speed > 0.01
  - strokes: number of shots taken
  - holeComplete: boolean, true when ball is in hole
  - aimAngle: current aim angle in radians
  - power: current power level (0-10)
  - charging: boolean, true while SPACE is held
  - ferrarLoaded: boolean, true when ferrari.glb is loaded
  - ferrariRotation: current Y rotation of Ferrari in radians
  - obstacleCount: number of obstacles on course (should be 2 bumpers + 1 ferrari = 3)
  - holePosition: {x, z} position of the hole
  - courseWidth: width of course (8)
  - courseLength: length of course (20)
  - par: par value for the hole (3)
  - gameStatus: string 'aiming' | 'moving' | 'complete'

## Animation Loop
- Use requestAnimationFrame
- Update ball physics each frame (use delta time, cap at 1/30s)
- Update Ferrari rotation
- Update power charging if SPACE held
- Update arrow helper visibility and direction
- Update __3D_STATE__ every frame
- Update HUD text elements every frame
physics_constraints: Ball moves on XZ plane with friction coefficient 0.985/frame. Wall collisions reflect velocity with 0.7 restitution. Ferrari collision uses sphere approximation (r=1.5) with 0.6 restitution. Ball sinks in hole when distance < 0.5 and speed < 2.0. Power ranges 0-10 linearly over 2 seconds of charging. Ball must stay within course bounds at all times.
